audition.description: Hear what you built, quietly, and how close it is to a reference, in one call: Kumi plays the part with Main silenced and hears each candidate track after its devices, compares it with the reference, then puts everything back. Up to 8 candidates are heard together in one real-time pass, so try several ideas at once (different instruments, chains, settings on separate tracks). Say where the part is: from_beat and beats in the Arrangement, or a Session clip per candidate (clip), which Kumi plays from the Arrangement for the render and removes after. A candidate can be the whole mix ({"mix": true}, on its own): what Main plays at from_beat, heard as quietly as a track; audition it against a reference to match a mix, changing EQ, compression and levels between rounds. Returns each candidate's closeness to the reference (0–100) with the biggest gaps in words, and what it heard. A silent render is reported, not compared. Without a reference it only listens.

candidates.description: The tracks to render, each on its own (a candidate sound, or the track to check), or the whole mix

mix.description: true: the whole mix (Main's output) instead of a track

beats.description: How long to render, in beats; a clip's length when left out, 8 at most by default

reference.description: What to match: an audio file's path or ~/…, or an audio clip's clipRef

reference_from_seconds.description: Where in the reference the part is

reference_seconds.description: How much of the reference to hear

focus.description: sound: one patch or hit (timbre, envelope, pitch); section: a part or mix (balance, density, rhythm too). Left out, by length

audition.renderDescription: Render an audio track's own clips (its recordings, a bounce) between two points to a file at once: offline and silent, no transport, no recording. It's the raw audio, before the track's devices; instruments, effects and the mix aren't in it (for those, audition, or record by resampling). Returns the file for listen, to hear it or compare it with a reference.

commands.description: Use Live's own commands, through its menus and keys, for what your other tools can't do: group or ungroup tracks, freeze, unfreeze or flatten a track, bounce a track or clip to audio without playing it (bounce_to_new_track, bounce_track_in_place), consolidate, convert an audio clip to MIDI (melody, harmony, drums), separate stems, slice to a MIDI track, save the Set (or collect all and save), save it as a new file (save_as with path), start a new Set (new_set) or open one (open_set with path), export audio or a MIDI clip. new_set and open_set replace the open Set: say what happens to its unsaved changes with save_current (ask the producer when they didn't say), and references from before are gone once it's open. Kumi fills Live's Save and Open dialogs on Windows only: on a Mac, ask the producer to save as or open a Set in Live. When a file is already at path, Live asks before replacing it: ask the producer, never answer it yourself. Never make or edit .als files yourself: Live calls a Set it didn't write corrupt. Give the command and what it works on (track, tracks side by side, or clip): Kumi selects it in Live, presses the command, and says what changed. For anything else Live's menus or keys do, give menu (the item's titles, ["Create", "Insert Silence"]) or keys (["cmd+e"]). When Live opens a dialog, its words and buttons come back: answer presses one. Live comes to the front for a moment. Prefer your other tools whenever one does the job.

command.description: One of Live's commands Kumi knows

track.description: The track it works on (its reference from this turn, or its name)

tracks.description: Tracks side by side (to group them), first to last

clip.description: The clip it works on: its clipRef from this turn (a Session clip; for converting to MIDI, an audio clip in Session or Arrangement), or "selected" for the one the producer selected in Live

path.description: The Set's file, a full path (Windows): where save_as saves it (its folder must exist; .als is added), which Set open_set opens, or where save puts a Set never saved

save_current.description: For new_set and open_set when the open Set has unsaved changes: yes saves them first, no discards them, cancel keeps the Set open

menu.description: Any of Live's menu items by its titles, ["Edit", "Freeze Track"]

keys.description: Keys to press in Live, one combination each: "cmd+shift+r", "down"

answer.description: Press this button of the dialog Live has open (OK, Export, Cancel…)

plugin.description: Work with a plug-in (Serum 2, Vital, Ozone, Pro-Q 4, Saturn 2, OTT, Supermassive, Decapitator, Pigments, Pro-L 2, or any other) the way its owner would. Read its guide before working on one. guide: what Kumi knows of it (its architecture, sound-design moves, what isn't a knob and how to get there), matched to its real parameter names, which of them Kumi can turn now (set those with set_device_parameter by name, in the plug-in's own units: "800 Hz", "-6 dB"), and how to get to the rest. wavetable: make a wavetable (keyframes of harmonics or shapes morphing frame to frame, or single cycles cut from a held note) into the plug-in's own wavetable folder, for its oscillator's menu.

device.description: The plug-in device (its deviceRef from this turn)

name.description: What to call it, as it shows in the synth's menu

keyframes.description: Frames it morphs through, first to last

count.description: Frames in all (morphing between keyframes); 64 for a sound cut from audio

from_audio.description: Cut single cycles from a held note instead
